preconditions.expression: all(isinstance(x, int) and x >= 1 and x <= 1000 for x in map(int, stdin.split()[1:]))
preconditions.description: The input consists of a single integer N (1 ≤ N ≤ 1000) on the first line, followed by N space-separated integers representing word lengths, each between 1 and 1000 inclusive.
The second line contains exactly N integers (word lengths) separated by spaces.

postconditions.description: If no valid set of words exists, output is exactly 'NO'. Otherwise, the first line is 'YES', followed by exactly N lines, each containing a binary string of the corresponding length from the input.

postconditions.expression: all(len(word) == int(length) for word, length in zip(stdout.splitlines()[1:], map(int, stdin.split()[1:])) if stdout.strip() == 'YES')
postconditions.description: Each output word's length matches the corresponding input length.

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() == 'YES' implies all(word in {'0', '1'} for word in stdout.splitlines()[1:])
postconditions.description: All output words consist only of the characters '0' and '1'.

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() == 'YES' implies all(not any(word.startswith(other) for other in words if other != word) for word in words)
postconditions.description: No output word is a prefix of another output word, where `words` is the list of output words (excluding 'YES').

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() == 'NO' implies not exists(words) such that all(len(word) == int(length) for word, length in zip(words, map(int, stdin.split()[1:])) and all(word in {'0', '1'} for word in words) and all(not any(word.startswith(other) for other in words if other != word) for word in words))
postconditions.description: If the output is 'NO', no valid set of words exists that satisfies the prefix-free condition and length constraints.
